scout_brief:
Focus theme: "Notebook management UX + durable notebook storage + operability (is-it-running) + container packaging" for arXMCP.

The operator wants to investigate four linked capability areas. Scout the 2026 state-of-the-art and the OSS/Docker landscape for CONCRETE, local-first-compatible options arXMCP could adopt, and measure each against what already exists.

ACCURATE CURRENT STATE (verified — do not re-litigate existence, assess the DELTA):
1. A SERVER-RENDERED FRONTEND ALREADY EXISTS but is minimal: server/routes/ui.py (Jinja2 HTML pages: notebook index + detail/browse, ar5iv preview from m8), frontend/templates/ + frontend/static/, and a REST API at server/routes/notebooks.py (/ui/api/notebooks/*: create notebook, upload PDF/HTML, per-kind 200MB/10MB cap). The design constitution (.claude/notes/06-mcp-server-design.md / CLAUDE.md) still says "no frontend exists, by design" — that is STALE; surface the drift. QUESTION: should arXMCP invest in a richer notebook-management frontend (add/remove papers, manage notebooks, see ingest/parse status, search UI), and if so what shape (keep server-rendered Jinja2+HTMX? a small SPA? a separate container?) WITHOUT violating local-first / loopback-only / the no-anthropic-SDK-at-runtime / pure-ASGI constraints?

2. NOTEBOOK STORAGE is local-filesystem only: per-notebook data under var/arxmcp/notebooks/<slug>/ (LanceDB + chunks + parsed HTML + pdfs), metadata in SQLite at var/arxmcp/cache/notebooks.db (server/notebooks_store.py), all under gitignored var/arxmcp/. It is NOT tracked code. The real gap: no portability / backup / durability / multi-device story; single-workstation. QUESTION: what LOCAL-FIRST-compatible storage upgrades exist — self-hosted S3-compatible object storage (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Garage), container volumes, litestream/SQLite replication, restic (E14 already ships restic backup — check), Docker named volumes vs bind mounts — to make notebook storage durable + portable + backed-up without a cloud dependency? HARD CONSTRAINT: local-first, no AWS S3 / requester-pays / multi-host-only dependency (this is an adversary axis in 08-security-observability-ops.md). Anything cloud-only is out; self-hosted-in-a-container is in.

3. OPERABILITY ("is the server running?"): /healthz (liveness), /readyz (readiness, 503 until BGE-M3 + LanceDB warm), /metrics (Prometheus) all exist. The gap is a HUMAN-FRIENDLY running/ready indicator (a status surface in the UI, a make status / CLI check, a docker healthcheck surfaced to the operator, a tray/desktop indicator?). QUESTION: lightweight operability patterns for a single-operator local MCP server.

4. CONTAINER PACKAGING: docker/Dockerfile.server exists (single image, non-root, tini, HEALTHCHECK on /readyz); there is NO docker-compose yet (infra/README.md is the E14 placeholder; infra/ has prometheus/observability/latexml/ca dirs). QUESTION: a docker-compose stack tying together the MCP server + notebook storage (volume or MinIO) + the frontend + observability (Prometheus/Phoenix already integrated) — what does a clean local-first compose stack look like, and does it unlock the storage + frontend + operability goals together?

Bias every finding toward CONCRETE deltas vs the current code, cite license + stars + last-commit for any OSS, respect the no-fork policy (ideas not import targets), and weigh every option against the local-first / loopback-only / single-workstation contract. Flag where the design constitution (notably the "no frontend by design" claim) needs updating.
